reviewer: GitHub Copilot (agent) - preview-grade review, not a substitute for a human art director
renders_reviewed: Playwright preview frames on Windows (scripts/frame-review.py --samples 12 --scan-fps 5 --fonts google); fonts are Google Fonts CSS stand-ins for the HyperFrames-bundled families. No HyperFrames MP4 render was available on this host.

criteria.question: One clear focal point per beat; reading order is obvious.
criteria.notes: Each beat pairs one copy block with one drawing state; copy enters first, then the drawing reacts. The 11.3 s sample catches the step-1 numeral mid-reveal with no other copy (transitional, acceptable).

criteria.question: Type roles are consistent; sizes respect the floor; no orphans or awkward breaks.
criteria.notes: Mono kicker / Playfair display / Inter body used consistently; accent italic carries the key word. Fixed during review: split added a space before the full stop in 'Chai, slowly.' and the square list wrapped 'green cardamom pods'. Portrait step bodies wrap to two lines with a short second line.

criteria.question: Layouts are intentional in every format (not stretched or cropped landscape).
criteria.notes: Landscape: editorial split. Portrait and square: stacked with the drawing as hero (enlarged during review; it previously filled about 40% of the width and left the lower half empty). Remaining weakness: portrait step scenes leave about 220 px unused above the reserved caption zone.

criteria.question: Holds match reading time; rhythm varies; nothing drags or rushes.
criteria.notes: Scene lengths meet the storyboard reading floors (studio.py validate) and frame-review found no line_unread findings. Rhythm alternates long (ingredients 6.8 s) and short (steps about 4 s) beats. Not judged against sound: this deliverable has no narration or music, and playback was only inspected as sampled frames.

criteria.question: All text is legible at delivery size with sufficient contrast.
criteria.notes: No text_below_floor or low_contrast findings in any format. Accent on paper is about 4.6:1 (style record contrast_checked). Smallest text is the mono quantity column.

criteria.question: Palette and texture follow the chosen style system and direction.
criteria.notes: editorial-light tokens throughout; ink line art with flat ingredient fills, one terracotta accent, static paper grain. Matches the selected 'ink-and-steam' direction in brief.json.

criteria.question: Each transition carries meaning or continuity; none are decorative filler.
criteria.notes: Page-turn wipe into the ingredients, hard cuts between recipe steps (deliberate card rhythm), liquid pour from the pan into the serving scene, match cut from the glass to the end-card mark. The pour and match cut were checked only as sampled frames, not in motion.

criteria.question: Motion vocabulary is consistent across scenes.
criteria.notes: Masked line rises for copy, pen-speed strokes for steam and glass, morphs for the liquid, and one persistent drawing across s1-s5.

criteria.question: No repetitive looping filler or motion without purpose.
criteria.notes: The only loops are steam wobble, flame flicker and the simmering surface, and each is tied to a heat state that ends at the pour. Grain is static, not boiling.

criteria.question: No unintended static stretches; intentional holds are marked.
criteria.notes: No dead_stretch findings in the 5 fps scan. The end card holds from about 28.7 s to 31 s, which the storyboard marks as hold-end.

criteria.question: No accidental overlaps, clipping or safe-area violations.
criteria.notes: No overlap, clipping or safe-area findings in three formats. In portrait and square the drawing deliberately rises into the top UI band; that region holds only decorative steam and spices, never text. Limits: sampled at 5 fps, and the fonts were stand-ins.

criteria.question: Clear opening, progression and ending; the last frame holds long enough.
criteria.notes: Title over a steaming pan, then ingredients, four numbered steps, the pour, serving, and an end card with about a 2.3 s hold. Frame 0 shows the drawn pan rather than the title, which is weaker as a thumbnail.

verdict: pass (preview-grade): repeat after HyperFrames MP4 renders on the M2 host with bundled fonts
pass_rule: Every criterion scored 1-5 with evidence (frame or contact-sheet paths); all >= 3 and mean >= 3.5.
